hook: Ritualo sits at a position that barely existed five years ago: the combined Chief Data and AI Officer function inside a cabinet-level foreign policy agency. Her career was built entirely on the federal data and performance management side, monitoring and evaluation, division chief, deputy CDAO, making her one of the few senior government AI officers whose path to the role ran through data governance and program evaluation rather than technology procurement.
name: Amy Ritualo

quote.text: Acting Chief Data and AI Officer, U.S. Department of State.

moniker: Acting Chief Data and AI Officer, U.S. Department of State

reading.body:
Amy Ritualo holds one of the most data-sensitive AI governance positions in the U.S. federal government, as Acting Chief Data and AI Officer at the Department of State, a role she reached through twenty-plus years of data governance and program evaluation rather than technology procurement.

The pattern in her career is consistent: each role added institutional scope to the same underlying discipline. Social science research gave way to applied policy analysis, then to federal data division management at high-volume agencies like DHS/USCIS, then to the State Department's combined data and AI function. The combined CDAO title itself is relatively new to government, and her occupying it signals that federal agencies are now treating data governance and AI oversight as a single problem rather than separate tracks.

For AI specifically, that framing matters. AI systems inside a foreign policy agency operate on some of the most sensitive information the government holds, and the governance questions, what data is collected, how it is evaluated, who is accountable for its use, are prior to any compute or infrastructure decision. Ritualo's background sits precisely in that prior layer. What this data does not address is the scope of any specific AI programs at the State Department, the resources allocated to the CDAO function, or how the acting designation affects the office's authority and continuity.
